done.why: I wanted to find treasure and keep it safe, and I did. Six treasures are in the trophy case and the score is 130. The trips back and forth were starting to feel like errands, so I stopped while things were going well.

about: An old white house sits on top of a huge cave system. You go down, take treasures from strange places like a drained lake, a sunken Atlantis room, a gallery and a temple, and carry them back up one at a time to a trophy case in the living room. Someone bars the trap door behind you, so the real puzzle is finding a way home with what you're carrying.

ending.what: No ending. I left at 130 of 350 points with six treasures in the case: egg, trunk of jewels, painting, platinum bar, crystal trident and ivory torch.

moments.note: 'walk around the house' worked, even though I typed it the way I'd say it to a person.
'gently take the egg' wasn't understood. I was trying to be careful with something fragile.
'go back to the house' wasn't understood. It only takes compass directions.
The trap door crashed shut behind me and someone barred it.
Trying to take the bar only gave back 'Bar bar ...'. I tried 'echo' on a hunch and it worked.
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it' kept coming back until I gave up the sword at turn 68.
Touching the mirror shook the room and moved me to a different Mirror Room.
The chimney message listed everything I was carrying and gave me the rule: me, my lamp and one thing more. Very clear.
A 'lean and hungry' gentleman with a bag came through the studio, found nothing worth taking and left. That was close.
The two Mirror Rooms and the two Caves look exactly alike. I got lost between them for several turns.
I typed 'pray' at the altar and suddenly I was outside in a forest. Great way to get out.
'go in the window' wasn't understood, but 'go west' took me inside.

wished: Say things in my own words, like 'go back to the house' or 'gently take the egg'
Ask why my sword was glowing
Ask which exits were open in the Round Room
Tell the two look-alike Mirror Rooms and Caves apart
Carry more than one thing up the chimney, or open the barred trap door from below

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: Suddenly I was trapped, and every trip after that was about getting home.
Funny and puzzling. The room itself was the puzzle.

lines.line: Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.
lines.why: A nudge that the sword I'd been relying on was what was weighing me down.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: It set the rule for my whole way of carrying treasure home: one at a time.

lines.line: A "lean and hungry" gentleman just wandered through, carrying a large bag. Finding nothing of value, he left disgruntled.
lines.why: Made me glad I'd already taken the treasures up to the case.

lines.line: There is an ugly person staring back at you.

fun.why: Getting the echo puzzle and finding the chimney route home felt clever, and praying my way out of the temple was a delight. It dipped during the repeated chimney trips.

engagement.why: Being trapped below and checking my score after each new treasure kept me going for a long time.

difficulty.why: Most of it I could work out. The hard parts were the strict wording, the weight limit and the look-alike rooms.

interestingness.why: The mirror jump, the chimney's carrying rule, the rope down the dome and the prayer that sends you outside all surprised me.

prose.why: Vivid and often witty, especially the egg, the gallery's vandals and the thief. Going back to a room often printed only its name, which made it harder to keep my bearings.
